377:
(a) It shall be a public nuisance to conduct a gathering of 15 or more persons on any private property in a manner which constitutes a substantial disturbance of the quiet enjoyment of private or public property in a significant segment of a neighborhood, as a result of conduct constituting a violation of law. Illustrative of such unlawful conduct is excessive noise or traffic, obstruction of public streets by crowds or vehicles, illegal parking, public drunkenness, public urination, public indecency, the service of alcohol to minors, fights, disturbances of the peace, and litter.
(b) A gathering constituting a public nuisance may be abated by all reasonable means including, but not limited to, an order requiring the gathering to be disbanded and citation and/or arrest of any law violators under any applicable county ordinances and state statutes.
(Ord. No. 2022-7, § 3, 8-11-2022)
378:
(a) When the sheriff's department intervenes at a gathering which constitutes a nuisance under this chapter, the premises at which such nuisance occurred shall be posted with a notice stating that the intervention of the sheriff's department has been necessitated as a result of a public nuisance under this chapter caused by an event at the premises, the date of the sheriff's intervention, and that any subsequent event within the period set forth below on the same premises, which necessities sheriff's department intervention, shall result in the joint and several liability of any guests causing the public nuisance, or any persons who own or are residents of the property at which the public nuisance occurred, or who sponsored the vent constituting the public nuisance as more fully set forms below. Any notice posted shall remain posted for a rolling calendar yen from the date the sheriff's department intervenes. For example, a notice posted on July 30th shall remain posted until July 29th of the following year.
(b) The notice posted under this section shall be no less than 8 x 14 in size and shall be neon green in color. The notice shall be constricted of a durable, weather resistant, adhesive material. The notice shall be affixed to the dwelling or structure and shall be posted in a conspicuous place. The sheriff or his designee shall determine the location in which such notice is posted in order to achieve both the security of the notice and its prominent display.
(c) The residents and owner of such property shall be jointly responsible for ensuring that such notice is not removed or defaced and it shall be a code violation carrying a penalty of a minimum, mandatory $100.00 fine in addition to any other penalties which may be due under this chapter if such notice is removed, obscured, or defaced.
(Ord. No. 2022-7, § 3, 8-11-2022)
379:
Notice of the intervention shall also be mailed via certified and regular U.S. mail to any property owner listed or the Washington County Tax Assessors' records. The notice shall advise the property owner that any subsequent such intervention within posting periods set forth in section 24-2(a) on the same premises shall result in liability of the property owner for all penalties associated with such intervention as more particularly set forth below.
(Ord. No. 2022-7, § 3, 8-11-2022)
380:
(a) If the sheriff's department is required to respond to a gathering constituting a public nuisance on the premises during any posting periods set forth in section 24-2(a), the following persons shall be jointly and severally liable for fines as set forth below:
(1) The person or persons who own the property where the gathering constituting the public nuisance took place, provided that notice has been mailed to the owner of the property as set forth herein and the gathering occurs at least 14 days after the mailing of such notice.
(2) The person or persons residing on or otherwise in control of the property where such gathering took place.
(3) The person or persons who organized or sponsored such gathering.
(4) All persons attending such gatherings who engage in any activity resulting in the public nuisance.
(5) Nothing in the section shall be construed to impose liability on the resident or owners of the premises, or sponsor of the gathering, for the conduct of persons who are present without the express or implied consent of the resident or sponsor, as long as the resident and sponsor have taken all steps reasonably necessary to exclude such uninvited participants from the premises, including landlords who are actively attempting to evict a tenant from the premises.
(b) Where an invited guest engages in conduct which the sponsor or resident could not reasonably foresee and the conduct is an isolated instance of a guest at the event violating the law which the sponsor is unable to reasonably control without the intervention of the sheriff's department, the unlawful conduct of the individual guest shall not be attributable to the sponsor or resident for the purposes of determining whether the event constitutes a public nuisance under this section.
(Ord. No. 2022-7, § 3, 8-11-2022)

392:
(a) In the construction of this article and of all ordinances and resolutions, the rules in this section shall be observed, unless such construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the county board of commissioners.
(b) The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
AASHTO means the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials, which publishes documents, including A Policy of Geometric Design (Green Book) and Roadway Design Guide.
Acceleration lane means a speed-change lane, including tapered areas, for the purpose of enabling a vehicle entering the roadway to increase its speed to a rate at which it can more safely merge with through traffic. Also called an "accel lane."
Access means entrance to or exit from land adjacent to a public road.
Angle of two-way driveway means the angle of deflection measured from the centerline of the nearest travel lane to the centerline of the driveway. An angle of 90 degrees is desirable.
Applicant means the person or organization that has applied for a permit.
Board of commissioners means the board of commissioners of Washington County, Georgia.
Clear zone. The roadside recovery area should remain free of hazards such as steep embankments, trees, poles, etc. Studies have indicated that on high-speed highways, over 45 mph, a width of 30 feet or more from the edge of the traveled way permits about 80 percent of the vehicles leaving a roadway out of control to recover safely.
Commercial driveway means any private entrance, exit, ramp, tunnel, bridge, side road or other vehicular passageway to any property used for commercial purposes, except a farm or dwelling house not exceeding a four-family capacity.
Commissioners means the board of commissioners of Washington County, Georgia.
County means Washington County, Georgia.
Deceleration lane means a speed-change lane, including tapered areas, for the purpose of enabling a vehicle that is making an exit turn from a roadway to slow to a safe turning speed after it has left the mainstream of faster-moving traffic. Also called a "decel lane"; it denotes a right turn lane or a left turn lane into a development.
Driveway width means the narrowest width of a driveway measured perpendicular to centerline of the driveway, from edge of pavement to edge of pavement or face-of-curb to face-of-curb where curb and gutter are installed.
Encroachment means the use of county rights-of-way by anyone other than county personnel or authorized agents for any specific purpose other than that generally intended.
GDOT means the Georgia Department of Transportation.
Governing body means the board of commissioners of Washington County, Georgia.
Guidelines. The proper design of driveways involves a number of design elements. Due to the complexity of the interaction between these design elements, exact design criteria cannot be specified for every possible situation. Therefore, design guidelines are included to assist the designer.
Island means a device used to separate or direct traffic in order to facilitate the safe and orderly movement of vehicles. An island may be a raised area that provides a physical barrier to channel traffic movements or a painted area.
Median crossover means an opening constructed in the median strip of a divided highway designed to allow traffic movements to cross from one side of the highway to the other. In some cases, the road department public works director may require the design to be such that some movements are physically prohibited.
MUTCD means the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (current edition).
NPDES means National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System.
Noncommercial driveway means. a driveway serving a school, government building, church, hospital or other noncommercial organization inviting public use. Provisions relating to commercial driveways will also generally be applicable to driveways serving these purposes.
O.C.G.A. means the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, as amended.
Owner, applied to a building or land, includes any part owner, joint owner, tenant in common, tenant in partnership or joint tenant of the whole or of a part of such building or land.
Permit means a legal document issued by the county authorizing an applicant to do specific work in county rights-of-way.
Residential driveway means any private passageway to any property used for dwelling purposes. However, if a driveway provides access for more than four dwelling units, it shall be considered a commercial driveway.
Right-of-way line means a line that defines the limits of the ROW of a public road as it relates to adjacent property.
Right-of-way miter means a right-of-way line at an intersection, which is parallel to neither road but forms a triangle with extensions of the ROW lines of the adjacent sides of the intersecting roads. The purpose of the ROW miter is to provide improved visibility for vehicles approaching the intersection by enabling the county to eliminate visual obstructions or provide room for a traffic signal support pole or guy wire. A driveway should never be allowed along the ROW miter.
Rights-of-way (ROW) means all land under the jurisdiction of, and whose use is controlled by, the county.
Road, street means and includes streets, avenues, boulevards, roads, and all other public highways in the county.
Roadway means the portion of a highway, including shoulders, for vehicle use.
Sight distance, as used in this article, refers to intersection sight distance, which is the distance that can be seen along the main roadway by the driver of a vehicle on the driveway. The distance is measured based on an eye height of 3.5 feet and an object height of 3.5 feet. Sight distance should be determined to provide adequate time for an entering vehicle to accelerate to within ten mph of posted speed limit, prior to being overtaken by approaching vehicles. (Refer to AASHTO, Green Book.)
Stopping sight distance means the sum of two distances: the distance traversed by the vehicle from the instant the driver sights an object necessitating a stop to the instant the brakes are applied and the distance required to stop the vehicle from the instant brake application begins. Stopping sight distance is measured based on an eye height of 3.5 feet and an object height of 2.0 feet.
Utility means all privately, publicly or cooperatively owned water distribution and sanitary sewer facilities and systems for producing, transmitting or distributing communication, cable television, power, electricity, light, heat, gas, oil, crude products, steam, wastewater and stormwater not connected with highway drainage, including river gages, fire and police signals, traffic control devices, and street lighting systems, which directly or indirectly serve the public or any part thereof. The term "utility" may also be used to refer to the owner of any above described utility or utility facility described in this definition.
Utility facility includes, but is not limited to, any and all poles, wires, guys, anchors, buried cable, conduit, pedestals, pipe lines, hydrants, valve boxes, manholes, casings, river gages and related fixtures authorized in the permit or agreement.
State Law reference— Computation of time, O.C.G.A. § 1-3-1; construction of definitions, O.C.G.A. § 1-3-2; meaning of certain words, O.C.G.A. § 1-3-3; time, O.C.G.A. § 9-11-6; official names of county governing authorities, O.C.G.A. § 36-5-20.
395: No mailbox or newspaper delivery box (hereafter referred to as a mailbox) will be allowed to exist on county rights-of-way if it interferes with the safety of the traveling public or the function, maintenance, or operation of the county road system. A mailbox installation that does not conform to the provisions of this regulation is an unauthorized encroachment under O.C.G.A. § 32-6-1. The location and construction of mailboxes shall conform to the rules and regulations of the United States Postal Service as well as to standards established by the county. County standards for the location and construction of mailboxes are available from the county.
396: Mailboxes shall be of light sheet metal or plastic construction conforming to the requirements of the United States Postal Service. Newspaper delivery boxes shall be of light sheet metal or plastic construction of minimum dimensions suitable for holding a newspaper. Mailbox supports shall not be set in concrete. A single four-inch by four-inch or four inch diameter wooden post or a metal post with a strength no greater than a two-inch diameter standard strength steel hollow pipe and embedded no more than 24 inches into the ground will be acceptable as a mailbox support. A metal post shall not be fitted with an anchor plat but it may have an anti-twist device that extends no more than ten inches below the ground surface. The post-to-box attachment details should be of sufficient strength to prevent the box from separating from the post top if a vehicle strikes the installation. Figures of acceptable attachment details and acceptable mailbox support assemblies are available from the county.
397:
The postal patron upon notification by the county shall remove any mailbox that is found to violate this policy. If such patron does not comply with the removal request it will be the county's prerogative to remove such mailbox. The following procedure may be used by the county to address an unacceptable mailbox:
(1) A letter shall be sent by certified mail to the postal patron stating that the patron has 30 calendar days to remove or modify the unacceptable mailbox.
(2) After 30 calendar days if the mailbox is not removed or made to comply, a second letter shall be sent by certified mail, advising the owner that the county will be removing the patron's mailbox after 15 calendar days.
(3) After the time limit on the second letter has expired, the county may schedule the removal of the mailbox.
(4) The removed mailbox will not be reinstalled but shall be placed out of the clear zone and next to the property line if possible. If placement of the removed mailbox is not possible out of the clear zone or on the patron's property by authorization, the mailbox shall be disposed of.
400: The purpose of the driveway permit process is to manage access on the county road system. Access regulations are necessary in order to preserve the functional integrity of the county road system and to promote the safe and efficient movement of people and goods.
401: A driveway permit is required prior to performing any construction work or nonroutine maintenance within the county rights-of-way. This generally includes residential and commercial driveways, but this may also include but is not limited to the following: grading, landscaping, drainage work, or construction of a development. Any revisions to any portion of existing driveways (i.e., widening and/or relocation that are within the county rights-of-way) shall also require a permit. In addition to being unlawful, performing the above-described work within the county rights-of-way without a permit shall entitle the county to barricade, displace, or otherwise close such driveway and to collect the costs thereof from the violator as provided for in this article.
402:
(a) Application to perform any construction or nonroutine maintenance work within county rights-of-way must be made to the county.
(b) Application for a permit under these regulations will be accepted only from the property owner, leaser or an official representing the company, organization, or group, which owns or leases the property abutting the ROW and upon which the driveway will be constructed. In the event the applicant leases the property to be served by the driveway, the lease should be for a period of at least three years; otherwise the permit must be issued to the property owner. In any case, written acknowledgement of the permit work must be obtained from the owner or his agent. In cases where a site with multiple owners is being developed by a single entity under a development agreement, the developer may apply for the permit. A copy of the development agreement between the developer and all affected property owners must be included with the application. The agreement must give responsibility for developing all affected driveways to the entity that is making application. When application is made by an agent of the owner or if the owner is a partnership or corporation, written authorization allowing the agent to act on behalf of the owner must be provided by applicant. An application for right-of-way encroachment may be obtained from the county.
403: For large developments, the applicant's engineer is encouraged to meet with the public works director early in the plan development process. A preliminary site plan is helpful to facilitate the exchange of information so the public works director can see the intent of the applicant. The preliminary site plan will also be useful in discussing the relevant requirements of these regulations.
404: Each applicant will provide a performance bond or letter of escrow to ensure that the authorized commercial driveway is accomplished in accordance with the approved permit. In cases of noncompliance, the bond will be used to offset the cost of correcting or removing uncompleted or unauthorized work, and to offset the cost of any damages incurred by the county or other parties as a result of the work or activities of the applicant in relation to this permit. The amount of the bond or letter of escrow is based on the estimated construction costs as determined by the county. A bond may be underwritten by a company housed outside of the state, if a state resident agent of said surety company countersigns. All letters of escrow must be from a bank housed in the state. Blanket performance bonds are acceptable. The blanket bond must contain the name of the owner or entity that is making application for permit. If the site is being developed on behalf of more than one owner under a development agreement, the surety must be in the name of the developer making application. A letter of credit from a bank housed in the state may be used for surety. It must be written without expiration or be written so as to automatically renew annually and the bank must agree to notify the county by registered letter at least 60 days prior to its expiration date if it does not intend to renew the letter of credit.
405: The applicant must submit construction drawings stamped by a registered engineer in the state with the permit application. Plans must conform to the minimum guidelines described herein. In addition, the applicant's engineer shall also use his judgment to prepare plans that conform to accepted guidance including but not limited to the most current edition of A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets published by AASHTO and the GDOT Regulations for Driveway and Encroachment Control. When submitting plans for review, the applicant must provide four sets of construction drawings. The county prefers plans with 24 inch by 36 inch sheet size or smaller. A plan review checklist containing information that should be shown on the construction plans is available from the county.
406: The plan review and application process is initiated when the applicant or their engineer submits an application permit, the necessary construction drawings to the county and the application fee as set from time to time by the board of county commissioners. When the county has completed its review of the permit and the plans and any necessary revisions have been made to their satisfaction, the applicant will be notified that his permit has been approved. The applicant is required to notify the county when the work will begin and when the work is complete. The works must be completed to the satisfaction of the county before the project can be accepted and the bond released. The project must be constructed according to the approved permitted plans. If, during the construction of the work, questions arise or unforeseen conditions are encountered, the contractor shall contact the county for consultation. The county will require as-built drawings if significant modifications are approved in the field. It is the responsibility of the property owner to provide routine maintenance of the pipe and driveway up to the roadway edge without making improvements to it as governed by the permit process including driveways installed prior to the effective date of the ordinance from which this article is derived.
407:
(a) The county administers residential driveway permits and the application fee, as set from time to time by the board of county commissioners. The county will advise the applicant regarding location of the drive, the size pipe if required to be placed under the driveway, and approve the grading plan from the outer edge of the road to the ROW line. Residential driveways are, as the name implies, driveways to private residences. Normally they are a minimum 20 feet wide. It is recommended that turnarounds be provided to avoid vehicles backing into the roadway. Under special circumstances, certain design vehicles require more width to safely negotiate a turn into or out of the drive without stopping and/or backing on the roadway. The county may also approve a driveway wider than 20 feet. If the driveway is paved, but without curb and gutter, there should be at least two-foot shoulder along the drive and around the radii before beginning the slope down to the drainage ditch. The front slope, back slope and the slope around the end of the drain pipe under the drive, if present, should be the same as if it were a commercial driveway. All side drain pipes larger than 48 inches must have an inlet and an outlet headwall. Only safety headwalls or those specifically approved by the county are allowed. On residential driveways this can be accomplished in several ways. If the pipe is corrugated metal and the applicant chooses to cut the end off to provide a 6:1 or flatter slope, he may install a concrete "collar" around the pipe end to provide stability and control erosion. Metal cross members must then be firmly attached to the pipe or collar at not more than two-foot spacing. The end treatment will be acceptable in lieu of attaching a prefabricated metal safety end treatment when applied to a residential driveway. When residential driveways are used to accommodate a semi-truck and trailer, the county will require the applicant to enlarge the driveway width to a minimum of 40 feet wide or larger if needed to appropriately permit ingress and egress of such semi-tractors, without the tractor entering into the ditch or right-of-way, and to be responsible for all additional driveway pipe and installation costs. It is the responsibility of the property owner to provide routine maintenance of the pipe and driveway up to the roadway without making improvements to it as governed by the permit process including driveways installed prior to the effective date of the ordinance from which this article is derived. Per this article, the county will no longer maintain or repair driveways. However, this article does permit the county to repair drop off areas immediately adjacent to the pavement or roadway surface. If, during routine county maintenance of a roadside ditch, a residential driveway pipe is discovered to be nonfunctional, it is the property owner's responsibility to replace the subject pipe. Should a driveway pipe create an unsafe roadway or right-of-way condition due to its nonfunction, the county may remove the driveway pipe to return the area to a safe condition. The removed driveway pipe shall be placed out of the clear zone and next to the property line if possible. If placement of the removed driveway pipe is not possible out of the clear zone or on the owner's property by authorization, the driveway pipe shall be disposed of.
(b) A typical residential driveway plan and profile and other special requirements is available from the county. All driveway pipes must be made of corrugated metal or concrete pipe or DOT approved double walled type S composite pipe, must be of sufficient grade to withstand vehicular traffic, and must be of sufficient diameter to allow for anticipated flow of water. No used pipes will be permitted for installation of a permanent driveway.
(c) The provisions of this section for residential driveways will not apply to driveways in place prior to enactment of the ordinance from which this section is derived, but will apply to whole new renovations of existing driveways, as well as to all new driveways.
(Res. No. 2015-2, 2-17-2015)
408: Utility driveways for accesses to utility sites such as power substations, water tanks, or telephone services sites are to be permitted by the county and should be treated much the same as a residential driveway for design and sight distance. The utility driveway must function in such a manner, which will allow the utility vehicle to pull completely off the roadway without stopping and backing into the drive or having to back out into roadway when exiting the driveway. The vehicle must not reduce the site distance for driveway located along the same section of roadway. A utility driveway will normally not count as one allowed access point along an applicant's frontage, depending on the length of frontage and safety considerations. A typical utility driveway layout is available from the county. The county will administer the issuance of permits and accompanying fee as set from time to time by the board of county commissioners. Relocation of an existing driveway by county, state, and federal entities, within the ROW will not require issuance of a permit.
409:
(a) Farm use, logging and mining driveways are to be permitted in a manner similar to utility driveways. A logging driveway will be a temporary driveway. Such driveways are regulated under article III of this chapter, pertaining to timber operations. However, if the driveway is to be installed to become a farm use or any other use driveway, then a permit will be required and all provisions and requirements for a driveway permit must be met. A mining operation may require a more substantial design to function properly. All temporary driveways, as with all other driveways, must sufficiently provide for proper water flow, and must not impede anticipated water flow.
(b) Signage requirements for driveways described in (a) above shall be the same as those for logging driveways as provided for in section 26-224(b).
(Res. No. 2015-2, 2-17-2015)
410:
No driveway approach or other improvements constructed on county ROW, as an exercise of the permit, shall be relocated or have its dimensions altered without the written permission of the county.
(1) A letter from the county approving the change should be obtained by the applicant who received a copy of the original permit.
(2) Parking is prohibited on county ROW except those instances where a temporary conditional special encroachment permit is approved for parking on the county ROW.
(3) Driveways should not be provided within the county ROW for purposes of parking, loading, servicing, etc.
(4) Geometric and safety requirements shall be maintained as stipulated in the permit and shall not be altered by the applicant.
(5) The applicant must take possession of an approved permit within 60 days of approval. If not, the permit will be canceled.
(6) Work under the permit shall begin within 90 days after approval. Failure to begin work will be cause for the permit to be canceled.
(7) Construction work authorized by an approved permit shall be completed within 12 months following approval of the permit. Permitted work not completed within 12 months, for just reasons, may be officially extended, by the county, for an additional six months. If the permitted work is not completed, action will be taken to secure the bond, escrow or letter of credit in order to complete the work or restore the county ROW.
(8) Once a permit has been canceled or voided, it cannot be reactivated or reinstated for any reason. A new permit must be submitted when the applicant is ready to begin work. This also includes the appropriate number of copies of up-to-date plans and all related documentation needed to review the application.
(9) New driveways to new businesses should not be opened for use by the traveling public until the final inspection and release of any bond or escrow by the county. In order to insure a timely release, the applicant is encouraged to coordinate all phases of work with the county.
(10) It is the responsibility of the property owner to provide routine maintenance of the commercial driveway up to the roadway edge of pavement without making improvements to it as governed by the permit process. Maintenance or replacement of the side drain pipe installed by the permittee will be their responsibility.
411: A median crossover constructed under a special encroachment permit or a commercial driveway permit becomes a feature of the roadway and the unconditional property of the county. The permit applicant or property owners and/or lessees adjacent to the ROW at the crossover site retain no ownership or legal interest therein. The county reserves the right and all authority to close, relocate or remove a crossover when such action is deemed necessary in the interest of public safety or efficiency of the roadway.
414: Before any public utility may be installed or relocated within county ROW or across county ROW, application for a permit shall be made to the county. The application for the permit shall contain a description of the location, nature of the public utility, direction, height or depth, distance and such other information as the county may reasonably require. The term "public utility," for any purposes of this section, shall include but shall not be limited to water lines, gas lines, sewer lines, pipelines, telephone lines, power lines, telecommunication cables, conduits and every other structure or device which by physical or electronic means conveys energy or substance, whether overhead or underground, along with supporting pedestals, poles and equipment.
415: It is the policy of the county that no public utility may occupy the county ROW unless sufficient space is available so that the free flow and safety of roadway traffic is not unduly impaired and the utility installation does not prevent the county from reasonably maintaining the roadways, structures, traffic control devices and other appurtenant facilities, and further provided that maintenance and operations of the utility do not jeopardize the traffic, or the highway structure or the maintenance thereof.
416: The county reserves the right to require the utility or entity that provides utility services to remove, repair, adjust or relocate any utility facilities installed within the county ROW of a road which the county has undertaken to improve, or intends to improve when, in the opinion of the county, the facility constitutes an obstruction or interference with the use of safe operation of such road by the traveling public or will interfere with such construction of maintenance. All utilities or entities providing utility services utilizing the county ROW are expected to react to the county's notification of proposed projects in time sufficient to assure removal or relocation so as not to adversely affect the county's construction schedule for the project. The utility owner may be held liable for any damages or excess costs of construction when delays are caused by failure of a utility to relocate within a reasonable time. Upon receiving written notification from the county to remove, relocate, repair or adjust its facilities which are using or occupying county ROW, which the county has undertaken to improve, the utility owner shall within 60 days thereafter begin arrangements for said removal, relocation, repair or adjustment in accordance with the written notification and instructions from the public works director. Should the owner fail to comply with such notice within a reasonable time sufficient to allow for engineering and other procedures reasonably necessary to the removal and relocation of the facilities, the county may give the utility a final notice directing that such removal be begun not later than ten days from the receipt of the final notice.
417: Such work shall be done in accordance with construction plans and specifications prepared by a registered engineer in the state. These plans are subject to the approval of county, and the work shall be performed under the review of the county. In all cases, it will be necessary for project plans to show the size, type and extent of utility facilities located on county ROW. Also, in all cases, it will be necessary for the construction plans to show any proposed adjustment or relocation of the utility facilities within the county ROW.
418:
(a) Protection of service. Utilities are to be located so as to minimize the need for future adjustment to accommodate future roadway improvements and to permit access for servicing such facilities with minimum interference to roadway traffic. The county may, on a case-by-case basis, require the utility to be encased.
(b) Longitudinal installations. Longitudinal installations are to be located on uniform alignment as near as practical to the ROW line, usually a five-foot offset, so as to provide a safe environment for traffic operation and preserve space for future roadway improvements or other utility installations. Underground pipeline installations are not to be located within the pavement or between the edge of pavement and the ditch or toe of front slope except where no other practical alternative exists and a special request for exception is submitted to and approved by the county.
(c) Highway crossing installations. To the extent feasible and practicable, utility line crossing of the highway shall cross on a line generally normal to the highway alignment.
(d) Clear roadside areas. The horizontal and vertical location of utilities within the roadway ROW limits shall conform to the clear roadside policies applicable for the system, type of roadway, and specific conditions for the particular roadway section involved. Aboveground utilities are a form of roadside obstacles, and their location must be consistent with the clearances applicable to all roadside obstacles for the type roadway involved.
(e) Preservation of safety, visual quality and maintenance efficiency. Full consideration shall be given to the measures, reflecting sound engineering principles and economic factors, necessary to preserve and protect the integrity and visual quality of the highway, its maintenance efficiency, and the safety of highway traffic.
419: No such pipe or main shall be laid upon any such ROW unless the same is at least 36 inches below the grade of such ROW, including 36 inches below the bottom grade of the ditch if crossing the ditch.
420:
(a) Construction methods are to be in accordance with the GDOT's Standard Specifications, current edition. Unsatisfactory restoration work shall be promptly corrected by the permit applicant. If necessary, unsatisfactory restoration work will be corrected by the county and its cost billed to the permit applicant.
(b) Drainage. Care must be taken in utility installations to avoid disturbing existing drainage facilities.
(c) Vegetative management on the ROW. Cutting and trimming of trees and shrubs growing on the highway ROW shall be held to the minimum required for installation and preservation of utilities. Generally, the maximum amount of clearance allowed for the utility is ten feet. Bush hogging will be allowed in areas where it is done on a frequent enough basis to avoid unsightly cuttings.
421: Traffic control for utility construction and maintenance operations shall conform to the MUTC. Individual traffic control plans may be required as directed by the county.
422: Whenever open trenching is required for the installation or maintenance of utilities within the ROW, the work shall be so scheduled that not more than 500 feet of trench shall be open at any one time. More restrictive controls may be imposed where conditions warrant. Insofar as possible work shall be scheduled so that open excavations will not be left overnight. Where trenches or pits are within the clear roadside areas and cannot be backfilled before leaving the job site, they shall be cordoned off and protected by reflectorized or lighted barricades as appropriate, or by other safety means as deemed appropriate.
423: The storage of materials on the county ROW within the clear roadside area is prohibited, except upon specific approval by the county when no other practical alternative exists. When such approval is given special safety precautions may be necessary for the protection of highway traffic. Such precautions will be stipulated in the permit or in a separate approval. Storage of materials outside the clear roadside area shall be temporary only, for a sufficient duration to facilitate their incorporation into the construction, which shall be expeditiously pursued.
424: No open cuts in pavement will be permitted except by special permission from the county when there is an emergency or for making a service tap on a line under the pavement when no other distribution line is available in the area where the service is required. In no event will an open cut be permitted when it is reasonably practical to bore, tunnel, etc., under the surface of the roadway.
425:
(a) It being the case that certain utilities, pipes, or lines that may run under county roads, may pose a hazard to said roads, utilities, lines, or pipes that run under a county road must be encased in a pipe which meets engineering standards or GDOT standards. The following list includes, but is not exhaustive, of all such utilities that must specifically meet these requirements: electric, gas, water, sewage, slurry, flowable suspendables, irrigation water, and any other pipe or line which may compromise the integrity of the road should failure occur.
(b) Additionally, any utilities, pipes, or lines to be run underneath county roads must take the shortest route, that is, must be run as perpendicular to the road it crosses as practicable.
426: The size of the disturbed area during installation shall be kept to a minimum.
429: This division describes the county's process and standard of review to allow other entities to grade, landscape or otherwise conduct roadside encroachment activity within, under, or over county ROW. The responsibility for maintenance of permitted roadside landscape activities that are constructed on county ROW by entities other than the county shall be borne by the permit entity.
430:
The elevation of the roadway may affect the ability of the adjacent property owner to fully utilize their property. In those cases, changes to the grade of the roadway ROW may be a less expensive option than the construction of a retaining structure outside the ROW. Where there is a documented benefit to the county, applicants may be permitted to grade the right-of-way to reduce the cost of development. Grading that requires tree removal within 500 feet of an outdoor advertisement sign is prohibited. The following general requirements for grading or excavating must be adhered to:
(1) Typically, if an earth embankment is in place, it may be lowered but not totally removed. In "cut" sections a berm of four feet to six feet in height may be required between the roadway ditch or curb and the right-of-way line to prevent headlight glare from adjacent properties onto the roadway.
(2) All slopes associated with allowable grading on county ROW shall be 4:1 or flatter.
(3) Reimbursement for soil removal from county ROW shall be at a rate determined by the county.
(4) Mitigation for tree removal or disturbance is required.
431:
Treatment of the roadside may be considered to conserve, enhance, and effectively display the indigenous character and quality of the environment it passes through by means of proper location, design, construction, and maintenance of their related features. All landscaping, roadside development and maintenance shall conform to the GDOT Standard Specifications, current edition, and any procedures and manuals maintained by the GDOT office of maintenance, including MOG 6160 (Roadside Development—Georgia Highway Landscape Guide). Maintenance management activities may include: selective tree and shrub pruning in conformance with industry standards for fine or standard pruning and/ or removal; introduction of predominately low maintenance native plants and subsequent maintenance of unmanaged natural areas or other maintained areas of the ROW. No crown reduction pruning or tree abuse shall be permitted. Any water placed on or in county roads or rights-of-way by means other than natural precipitation is prohibited, other than the temporary spraying of roads to clean off accumulated mud. Except that, on unpaved county roads, irrigation water shall be allowed to hit roads if the person responsible places reflective warning signs at least 1,000 feet but no more than 1,200 feet prior to the area in which the irrigation occurs, and provided that said signs are approved by the county and removed no later than 24 hours after the irrigation stops. In the event spraying of a paved road to clean off accumulated mud does occur, proper safety measures must be utilized including the placement of warning signs indicating wet or slippery roads, or the use of other safety measures as deemed appropriate.
(Res. No. 2014-11, 8-14-2014)
432:
(a) The county will give consideration for approval of grading and/or landscaping activities based on compatibility with primary use and protection of the county's investment in the roadway facility. Beneficial reasons for encroachment activity may include, but are not limited to the following:
(1) Improved shoulder or clear zone distances.
(2) Improved drainage.
(3) Elimination of hazards and/or guardrail.
(4) Reduced maintenance costs.
(b) Applications are reviewed to determine the impact of the encroachment on the following:
(1) Safety of motorists, pedestrians, and workers.
(2) Design, construction, operation, maintenance, or integrity of the highway system.
(3) Aesthetic.
(4) Environment.
(5) Existing drainage.
(c) An encroachment activity may be considered when there is no cost to the county and all negative real value changes to the ROW are reimbursed to the county. Items of real value include the costs for recurring maintenance, material removed, and the value of trees and other vegetation. Care must be taken to prevent encroachments that devalue county ROW. The applicant shall be responsible for all liability for personal injury and property damages for permitted activities. Permit applications may be acceptable if all the following items are satisfied:
(1) The county is compensated for removal of material or use of the ROW.
(2) No safety hazard is created.
(3) No additional maintenance is created.
(4) No additional liability is assumed by the county.
(5) No transportation use restriction is created.
(6) No unwanted easement or other permanent ROW encumbrance is created.
(7) Activity will not be detrimental to the future use or expansion of the roadway.
(d) Permits will not be issued for encroachments if any of the following conditions exists:
(1) The activity adversely affects the safety, capacity or integrity of the county road system.
(2) The activity compromises or jeopardizes the drainage system on the ROW.
(3) The activity is to grade, remove or prune trees, shrubs and groundcovers when the county has determined that the activities will significantly disrupt natural systems, roadside aesthetics, or have other negative impacts on the operation of the highway. Structural integrity and tree health as well as vegetative ground cover for erosion control are of primary importance to the maintenance of the ROW and shall not be compromised for purposes of grading to reduce development costs, day lighting, or landscaping development activities.
(4) Tree removal and/or grading for "daylighting" purposes when there is no benefit to the ROW or traveling public.
(5) The applicant has not complied with the provisions of prior permits.
433: All plans developed for a special encroachment permit shall be submitted to the county for review. In most cases, the applicant will be best served by providing four sets of preliminary site plans for an initial review. Upon receipt of an application with plans, the county shall check to ensure that plans and related documents are complete and meet the requirements of this procedure. The applicants will have 90 calendar days to revise the plans, should the county generate comments. New application submittal packages will be required after 90 days. The applicant shall submit two copies of the revised plans for final review by the county. If modifications to the plan are beyond the comments made or a major modification is made for other reasons, the plan should be treated as a preliminary submittal and rechecked.
434: When submitting plans for review, the applicant must provide four sets of construction drawings. The county prefers plans with 24 inch by 36 inch sheet size or smaller. A plan review checklist containing information that should be shown on the construction plans is available from the county.
435:
The owner of a nonconforming special encroachment upon notification by the county shall remove any encroachment that is found to violate this policy. If such owner does not comply with the removal request it will be the county's prerogative to remove such encroachment. The following procedure may be used by the county to address a nonconforming special encroachment such as mailboxes, driveways, grading/excavating, etc.:
(1) A letter shall be sent by certified mail to the owner stating that the owner has 30 calendar days to remove or modify the nonconforming encroachment.
(2) After 30 calendar days if the nonconforming encroachment is not removed or made to comply, a second letter shall be sent by certified mail, advising the owner that the county will be removing the owner's nonconforming encroachment after 15 calendar days.
(3) After the time limit on the second letter has expired, the county may schedule the removal of the nonconforming encroachment.
(4) The removed nonconforming encroachment will not be reinstalled but shall be placed out of the clear zone and next to the property line if possible. If placement of the nonconforming encroachment is not possible out of the clear zone or on the owner's property by authorization, the nonconforming encroachment shall be disposed of.
(5) A violation of this section is punishable by a fine up to $1,000.00 and or 60 days imprisonment. Additionally, any cost associated with such removal will be placed as a lien on the subject property.
438: The purpose of this article is to provide regulations governing the use of public roads by persons engaged in timber operations in the county and establish procedures for the conduct of such operations in order to ensure the public safety and to protect the county roadways and environment.
439:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Permit means the permit issued by the road department for timber operations.
Permit holder means the applicant on the permit. The permit holder is the entity responsible for all operations at the harvest site. Either a buyer or timber harvester may be the permit holder.
Public works director means the public works director of Washington County.
Road department means the Washington County Road Department.
Surety bond means a cash bond, irrevocable letter of credit, or bond issued by a licensed surety authorized to do business in the state.
Timber means softwood or hardwood trees harvested for commercial purposes.
Timber harvester means any person, firm, or corporation engaged in timber operations.
Timber operations means buying, cutting, harvesting, loading, and or hauling timber.
440:
(a) No person shall undertake timber operations without first obtaining a permit from the county road department and posting a surety bond. Bonds will be posted at the county road department. Permits will similarly be obtained at same department at 1862 Kaolin Road, Sandersville, GA. Note: All timber operations in the county must be permitted regardless of location.
(b) All permits will be effective for a period of six months, after which they will automatically expire.
(c) A bond may cover more than one location, but each separate tract harvested must have its own permit.
(d) The permit application will be made in person at the county road department.
(e) The bond to be posted shall be $2,500.00 for tracts less than five acres, and $5,000.00 for all tracts five acres or greater.
(f) The permit applicant must present at the time of application a map of the tract to be harvested. Such map must indicate the map and parcel number and property lines for the tract to be harvested. In addition, the map must indicate the road the tract is located on, or the nearest public road to the tract, plus the nearest public road intersection.
(g) Decisions regarding the ingress or egress route for the timber operations are at the discretion of the county road department and are made based on road conditions, public safety, population density, road structures, and other factors. However, it is the sole responsibility of the permit holder to safely navigate and execute ingress and egress form the harvest site.
(h) It is recommended that the county road department be consulted in advance, prior to execution of buy/sell agreements, should it appear that ingress or egress to a state road will be of concern.
(i) A copy of the permit should be posted on site at the harvest site entrance. The county road department shall likewise maintain a copy on file. The map submitted with the application process shall become part of the permit and shall similarly be posted at the harvest site.
(j) Any changes to the permit needed, including ingress and egress route, dates, or otherwise, must be reported immediately to the county road department. No changes can be made until approved by the road department.
(k) All permits shall carry the following language underneath the signature line:
"BY SIGNING THIS APPLICATION, PERMIT HOLDER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT HE/SHE IS RESPONSIBLE FOR FULL COMPLIANCE WITH ALL CONDITIONS OF THIS PERMIT, AND IS FURTHER RESPONSIBLE FOR ANY VIOLATIONS BY ALL WORKERS, LOGGERS, TRUCKERS, HARVESTERS, ETC., OF THE CONDITIONS OF THIS PERMIT. SAID PERMIT HOLDER IS ALSO AWARE OF POSSIBLE FINES AND FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITIES FOR VIOLATIONS OF CHAPTER 26, ARTICLE III, OF THE CODE OF WASHINGTON COUNTY."
441:
(a) Driveways.
(1) All ingress and egress driveways shall be no less than 40 feet wide, shall be considered a temporary driveway (unless a permit for a permanent driveway is applied for) and shall not impede anticipated water flow. All driveways must utilize a proper pipe of sufficient diameter as noted below, unless the director of public works or his designee specifically approves a driveway without a pipe based on the topography of the logging site.
(2) Any existing driveways to be utilized that are less than 40 feet wide must be upgraded to a minimum of 40 feet prior to commencement of timber operations.
(3) Any pipes in driveways must be at least 40 feet wide. Any existing pipes less than 40 feet wide must be upgraded to 40 feet prior to commencement of timber operations. Any pipe used must be of sufficient diameter to provide for proper water flow, and shall not impede anticipated water flow.
(4) In addition to the 40-foot width requirement, all ingress and egress driveways must provide sufficient turning radius to permit ingress or egress without trucks going off the road, onto the rights-of-way or ditches. Driveways that do not provide sufficient turning radius to alleviate trucks from going off the road (thereby causing damage to the road shoulder or pavement edge) may be required to be wider to accommodate such ingress and egress.
(5) All ditches and pipes surrounding the driveway and in the harvest area must be kept clear and free of obstacles so as to not inhibit water flow.
(6) At all times ingress and egress driveways must meet the standards of the county for ingress and egress to a county road. If ingress and egress is to a state road, then the requirements of the state department of transportation must be met.
(b) Signage.
(1) Signs must be posted 500 feet in both directions from the point where the driveway enters a public road. Such signs shall state TRUCKS ENTERING ROADWAY or other appropriate language.
(2) If the point where the driveway enters a public road is within 500 feet of said road's intersection with another public road, additional signage shall be posted on the intersecting road. Such signs shall be posted 500 feet from such intersection and shall contain the language described in the section 26-224(b)(1).
(Res. No. 2015-2, 2-17-2015)
442:
(a) All trucks shall utilize the prescribed ingress and egress route as specified in the permit. Such route shall be used whether trucks are loaded or unloaded, and whether coming to or leaving the harvest site/timber operation location. The permit holder must advise all truck drivers of the prescribed route. It is the responsibility of the permit holder that all truck drivers comply with this route.
(b) The prescribed route shall direct all trucks from the site to the nearest state road or county truck route. Such trucks shall then stay on state roads or county truck route until exiting the county.
(c) No non-truck routes or county roads shall be utilized to cut off travel distance, or to digress from a state road or from the prescribed route outlined in the permit.
(d) If circumstances such as road work, bridge load requirements, heavily congested or populated areas, or other circumstances arise, the director of public works may designate a different route as appropriate to accommodate such circumstances.
(e) Any request for a special route, other than as prescribed, must be discussed with and approved by the director of public works prior to the application for a permit.
443:
(a) No county or state or federal road shall be obstructed by any equipment or truck in relation to timber operations.
(b) At no time shall vehicles or equipment park on the roads or rights-of-way.
(c) No mud shall be carried onto a paved road by any truck or equipment. Precautions such as gravel or other means shall be utilized in the event it appears mud is being carried onto paved roads.
(d) During times of inclement weather, logging operations shall not be undertaken if so doing will cause damage to the public roads of the county, or make roads impassable to the traveling public.
(e) No logger, harvester, truck driver, or permit holder shall violate any of the terms of the logging permit.
(f) The permit will be valid for six months from date of issuance. No operations shall take place after the expiration of the permit.
444:
(a) Any violation of the provisions of this article shall constitute a violation of county ordinance punishable by a fine of up to $1,000.00 and or 60 days in jail.
(b) The road department, at its discretion, may issue a written warning to anyone in violation of this article, and to permit the permit holder to immediately rectify the alleged violation, prior to issuance of a citation.
(c) In all cases, a subsequent violation of any provisions of this article, whether at the same logging site or a subsequent logging operation, and whether involving the same or other type of violation under this article, shall be handled by means of citation.
(d) Notwithstanding the penalty provisions of this article, any violation of this article may also be addressed by a noncriminal civil fine.
(e) Such noncriminal civil fines shall be equal to ten percent of the bond for each violation.
(f) Further, in addition to any penalties of this article, the permit holder shall immediately rectify any violation of this article, or shall immediately cease operations at the harvest site until corrections have been made and approved by the road department.
446:
Footnote 2:
Editor's note— Ord. No. 2025-1, adopted May 5, 2025, set out provisions intended for use as art. II, div. 1—3. For purposes of classification, and at the editor's discretion, these provisions have been included as art. IV, div. 1—3.
448:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Affected parcel owners means owners of parcels that abut the county road being petitioned to be renamed or closed excluding county-owned parcels.
Affected tenants mean individuals or entities that may not own the parcel abutting the county road to be renamed but who may reside or have a business on said parcel. The determination of the number affected tenants shall be made by available county records at the time.
Applicant means the individual initiating a road renaming or road closure. Applicants must be a fee simple owner of a parcel abutting the subject county road to be renamed or closed.
Parcel means a definitive platted lot or other tract of land shown as a tax parcel on the most recent official tax map of Washington County, Georgia, and assigned its own unique tax parcel number by the Washington County Board of Assessors office.
Petition means a petition which has been signed by 90 percent of affected parcel owners who are in favor of the road or alley renaming or closing.
Reimbursement fee means average estimated fees to reimburse the county for the costs of renaming or closing a public county road including, but not limited to, costs for: (1) advertising; (2) signage materials and installation; and (3) certified mail and postage.
(Ord. No. 2025-1, 5-5-2025)
451:
The decision to change the name of a county road within the Washington County shall only be considered upon receipt of a completed petition as described below. The decision to rename county road shall be made by the sole discretion of the BOC.
(Ord. No. 2025-1, 5-5-2025)
452:
(a) Pre-submittal meeting required. An applicant requesting the renaming of a county road, or a portion thereof, shall first schedule an appointment and meet with the county administrator or his designee to discuss the nature of the request, reimbursement fee, the applicable county procedures and requirements, and other items that may be required as part of the submitted request. Following the meeting, the county administrator or his designee shall provide the amount of the reimbursement fee to the applicant. An application must be submitted to the county containing the following information:
(1) The name, signature, address, and contact information of the applicant.
(2) The proposed new name of the subject county road, or portion thereof; and
(3) A justification for the name-change request.
If the proposed road is to be named after a person or persons, such individual(s) must meet the following criteria:
(4) They must be deceased.
(5) They must have provided "extraordinary public service or some exemplary contribution" to the public; and
(6) They must be associated with the community where the subject county road, or portion thereof is located. Prior to the commencement of the petition process detailed in the ordinance, the reimbursement fee must be paid, and a complete application must be provided to the county administrator or his designee.
(b) Submittal of petition. The applicant is responsible for collecting the information required on the petition from all affected parcel owners. The applicant shall have up to 60 days from to collect the required, 90 percent of affected parcel owners' signatures on the petition in favor of renaming the county road. The petition shall be returned to the county administrator and the county's formal review and processing will commence. Copies of the petition and other relevant materials shall then be distributed to county departmental staff and other relevant parties as determined by the county administrator, for review and comment. The county administrator or his designee shall then forward a copy of the petition and other relevant materials to the county clerk and schedule the request for a public hearing with the county commissioners as properly advertised in accordance with subsection (c) below.
(c) Notice of public hearing. To provide notice of the public hearing for the consideration of the petition by the BOC, the county administrator, or his designee shall:
(1) Inform all affected parcel owners and affected tenants via certified mail that the petition has met the requisite 90 percent threshold to be considered by the BOC and provide the date of the public hearing when the petition will be considered.
(2) Install public hearing signage at either end of the subject county road to be renamed at least ten calendar days prior to public hearing.
(3) Cause a legal notice of the public hearing to be published in a newspaper of general circulation within the county a minimum of two separate times at least ten calendar days before the scheduled public hearing before the BOC.
(4) Utilize available digital media, including but not limited to the Washington County social media platforms, to provide notice of the public hearing at least ten days prior to public hearing. All notices shall contain the date, time and place of the public hearing, a location description of the street, alley, or portion thereof to be renamed, and both the existing and proposed names. After the advertisement requirements have been met, the proposed county road renaming will be placed upon the BOC meeting agenda for approval or denial.
(d) Conduct of the public hearing. The public hearing shall begin with a report from the county administrator detailing the petition process and any concerns of county staff. Both proponents and opponents of the petition shall be provided equal opportunity to speak in favor or opposition. The chairman may limit the presentation of those for and against a petition to a reasonable length of time.
(e) Criteria and timing of decision. The renaming of a county road shall be in the sole discretion of the BOC but with consideration of the following non-exclusive factors:
(1) The proposed new county road name;
(2) Unnecessary costs, expenses and trouble to owners and residents; and
(3) Potential confusion in providing essential services such as emergency response, utility distribution, trash collection, and mail delivery.
The BOC shall take final action after the conclusion of the public hearing or within 30 days thereof.
(f) Post-notification and effective date of change. 456:
(a) Pre-submittal meeting required. An applicant requesting the closing of a county road shall first schedule an appointment and meet with the county administrator or his designee to discuss the nature of the request, responsibility for payment of reimbursement fee, the applicable county procedures and requirements, and other items that may be required as part of the submitted request. The county administrator or his designee shall inform the reimbursement fee amount to the applicant for their consideration. Prior to the commencement of the petition process detailed in subsection (b), the reimbursement fee must be paid, and a complete application must be provided to the county administrator or his designee.
(b) Submittal of petition. The applicant is responsible for collecting the information required on the petition from all affected parcel owners. The applicant shall have up to 60 days from to collect the required, 90 percent of affected parcel owners' signatures on the petition in favor of closing the county road. The petition shall be returned to the county administrator and the county's formal review and processing will commence. Copies of the petition and other relevant materials shall then be distributed to county departmental staff and other relevant parties as determined by the county administrator, for review and comment. The county administrator or his designee shall then forward a copy of the petition and other relevant materials to the county clerk and schedule the request for a public hearing with the county commissioners as properly advertised in accordance with subsection (c) below.
(c) Notice of public hearing. To provide notice of the public hearing for the consideration of the petition by the BOC, the county administrator, or his designee shall:
(1) Inform all affected parcel owners via certified mail that the petition has met the requisite 100 percent threshold to be considered by the BOC and provide the date of the public hearing when the petition will be considered.
(2) Install public hearing signage at either end of the subject county road to be closed at least ten days prior to public hearing;
(3) Cause a legal notice of the public hearing to be published in a newspaper of general circulation within the county a minimum of two separate times at least ten calendar days before the scheduled public hearing before BOC.
(4) Utilize available digital media, including but not limited to the Washington County social media platforms, to provide notice of the public hearing at least ten days prior to public hearing.
(5) All notices shall contain the date, time and place of the public hearing, a location description of the county road to be closed. After the advertisement requirements have been met, the proposed county road closure will be placed upon the BOC meeting agenda for approval or denial.
(d) Conduct the public hearing. The public hearing shall begin with a report from the county administrator detailing the petition process and any concerns of county staff. Both proponents and opponents of the petition shall be provided equal opportunity to speak in favor or opposition. The chairman may limit the presentation of those for and against a petition to a reasonable length of time.
(e) Criteria and timing of decision. Closures of county roads shall only be made upon the determination that said county road has ceased to be used by the public to the extent that no substantial public purpose is served by it or that its removal from the county road system is otherwise in the best public interest. The closure cannot result in a parcel having no public right-of-way to provide egress and ingress to said parcel. The BOC may take final action after the conclusion of the public hearing or within 30 days thereof.
(f) Post-notification and effective date of change. The closing of any public county road shall be effective 60 days after final action or as otherwise stipulated by the BOC at the time of final action. Within seven calendar days of final action, official notification of an approved closing of a county road shall be sent regular mail by the county clerk to the owner of each parcel of land abutting the county road portion that was closed.
(g) Transfer of ownership. Unless otherwise stipulated by BOC, the closure of a county road shall result in the transfer of ownership of said county road in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 532-7-4, O.C.G.A. § 36-37-6 and/or applicable law. The costs of the transfer shall be borne by the grantee[s] unless otherwise required by law. Additionally, if the county road is also vacated by the county commissioners and resulting in a transfer of ownership and realignment of property boundaries, then such action shall also result in compliance with the subdivision re-platting requirements of the county's land development.
(h) Declination by BOC. If the BOC declines to rename county road, or if the petition is abandoned by the applicant, the applicant shall be reimbursed the unutilized portion of the reimbursement fee within 30 days of declination or petition abandonment. The county shall not be responsible for the redistribution of monies fundraised to cover the reimbursement fee. Re-applications for the changing of a specific county road name shall not be considered for a period not to exceed one year following petition abandonment or declination by the BOC.

(a) Public compactor/dumpsters.
(1) The board of commissioners may designate areas in the county where compactor/dumpsters, intended to be for public use, shall be located and maintained. These compactor/dumpsters may be located on public property, along the right-of-way of public roads and streets, or on private property with the express written consent of the owner and tenant in legal possession of the property, and may be located in such a manner that there is a minimum danger of the spread of noxious odors and the detrimental effect on the environment is minimal.
(2) It shall only be lawful for property owners or residents for whom the county garbage fee is paid to place or deposit any garbage, refuse, litter, household trash or other material of any kind in these compactor/dumpsters.
(3) It shall only be lawful to place household garbage and trash in said dumpsters. More specifically, it shall be strictly unlawful for anyone, including county residents, to place any garbage or trash or material in such dumpsters or on the grounds surrounding such dumpsters, other than household garbage or household trash as defined.
(4) The compactor/dumpster site shall carry a placard or sign stating that they are solely intended for the use of residents of county, and that it is unlawful to deposit anything other than garbage or household trash therein.
(5) It shall be unlawful to place or deposit industrial waste or construction/demolition wastes in these compactor/dumpsters unless they are specifically designated for such use by the board of commissioners.
(6) It shall be unlawful to place or deposit any hazardous solid wastes of any kind in the compactor/dumpsters.
(7) It shall be unlawful for any person to dispose of or discard in the compactor/dumpster any hypodermic injection devices before first breaking, disassembling, destroying or otherwise rendering inoperable and incapable of reuse, any hypodermic syringe, needle, instrument or device and without safeguarding the disposal thereof by wrapping or securing same in a suitable manner so as to avoid the possibility of causing injury to the collection personnel.
(8) It shall be unlawful to deposit ash of any type in the compactor/dumpsters.
(9) It shall be unlawful to deposit highly combustible material in the compactor/dumpsters.
(10) It shall be unlawful to place or deposit material or substance governed or regulated as a noxious or toxic material by any governmental agency or which would pose a hazard to the health, safety and well-being of the collection personnel or residents of the county, or which could contaminate the ground or surface water of the county, or which would pose a danger to the wildlife of the county, shall be placed or deposited in the compactor/dumpsters.
(11) It shall be unlawful to place or deposit any garbage or household trash in the compactor/dumpsters without first placing and securing such in a garbage bag of suitable strength and thickness. Objects which could puncture the garbage bag in the course of the ordinary and intended use thereof shall be wrapped or protected so that the bag shall remain intact.
(12) It shall be unlawful to place or deposit garbage or household trash on the ground adjacent to the compactor/dumpsters or in any location other than the compactor/dumpsters, unless otherwise directed and except that recyclable materials may be placed in designated containers where provided. Any person using the compactor/dumpsters shall clean up any spills caused by his use of the compactor/dumpsters and shall not drop or discard any garbage or household trash in the area surrounding the compactor/dumpsters.
(13) Dead or live animals shall not be placed or deposited in or around the compactor/dumpsters.
(b) Public construction/demolition wastes landfill and solid waste landfill.
(1) The county, through the board of commissioners, may operate and maintain public landfills located on county property in compliance with all applicable state and federal laws and regulations, and may adopt procedures, rules and regulations to govern the operation and use of construction/demolition wastes landfills and sanitary landfills.
(2) Public sites approved for the disposal of solid wastes shall be identified by appropriate directional signs posted near the roadside and at the location of the county solid waste landfill.
(3) Such sites shall be maintained in use until permanently closed, at which time, additional authorized sites may be opened and publicized by posting and through public advertisements.
(4) The board of commissioners shall restrict certain sites or portions thereof to a specific type or types of solid wastes. The board of commissioners may adopt operational policies concerning the separation, storage and use of recyclable materials. Citizens are encouraged to practice source separation of specific types of solid wastes for disposal at specific sites by different methods.
(5) Commercial collectors, including yard maintenance men, may use the public designated landfill upon the payment of applicable fees, if any, established by the board of commissioners.
(6) Residents of the county and businesses located in the county, other than commercial collectors, may use the public designated landfills upon payment of a fee to be set by the board of commissioners, in accordance with the regulations for the particular site and under the instruction of the site attendant.
(7) Municipalities located within the county may use the public landfill upon the payment of applicable fees, if any, established by the board of commissioners.
(8) Solid wastes generated outside the county will only be accepted at any disposal site operated by the county with the approval of the board of county commissioners by majority vote.
(9) The landfill site shall be operated on the days established from time to time by the board of commissioners. During the hours designated by the board of commissioners or their designate, acceptable solid wastes generated in the county shall be received for disposal from any resident of the county. No fee shall be charged to residents for whom the county garbage fee is paid.
(10) No person shall enter the landfill except when an attendant is present and during the hours and days prescribed in this article. All materials delivered and deposited for disposal in the landfill shall immediately become the property of the county, unless the county refuses any such material at the time it is presented for deposit in the landfill, or the county, within a reasonable time, notifies the depositor of the unacceptability of the materials and to retrieve the materials.

(a) Private collectors. It shall be unlawful for any person to collect solid wastes within the county except from his or her own residence, business or industrial plant, without first having obtained a proper permit from the state department of natural resources. This provision shall not prohibit the utilization of centralized recycling collection facilities by persons not in the business of recycling.
